decisionBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET. Used only by POST /v1alpha1/human-tasks/{id}/decision — every other operation in this API is authless by phase-1 design (spec decision c45).

info.description:
The Culture Nodes control-plane API (docs/initial-design/culture-nodes-prd-spec.md §12.1, §15.1): workflow publication, run orchestration, the append-only work ledger, and review transactions. group: nodes.culture.dev/v1alpha1.
Phase 1 runs authless by design (spec decision c45): this API carries no authentication or authorization of its own and is meant to run behind a private network. Every operation is reachable by anyone who can reach the listener. Do not expose this API on a public network without a fronting proxy that adds authentication.
Every error response, on every operation, uses the Error schema below — the same {code, message, remediation} shape internal/clifmt.CliError renders for the CLI — with the HTTP status line carrying the specific condition.
info.title: nodes.culture.dev/v1alpha1

get.description: Always `200` once the process is serving requests. Does not touch the database.

parameters.description: Filter to "pending" or "decided". Omitted returns every status.
parameters.name: status

404.description: No human task has this id.

post.description:
Validates outcome against the task's own allowed_outcomes (PRD §9.9), records the decision as a human-authority review through the same atomic, ledger-version-guarded review transaction PRD §10.8's review commit uses, transitions the waiting_human node run, and routes the edge the outcome selects — all in one transaction, or none of it. A task decides exactly once: a second decision on an already-decided task is refused with 409 rather than resuming the run again.
Unlike every other operation in this API — authless by phase-1 design, spec decision c45 — this one requires a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) matching the server's configured decision secret (`NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET`): a decision here writes human authority into the run's ledger on whoever's behalf presents the token. An unauthenticated or wrongly authenticated request is refused with 401 before the body is even read.

200.description: The decision was committed and the run resumed (or ended, if the routed edge reached an end node).

400.description: The request is malformed, or outcome is not one of the task's allowed_outcomes.

401.description: No bearer token was presented, it does not match the configured secret, or no secret is configured at all.

404.description: No human task has this id.

409.description: The task is already decided, or expected_ledger_version no longer matches the run's current ledger version.

get.description:
The cross-run "jobs timeline" listing (task t11): every node run in this namespace, not scoped to one run — unlike the `node_runs` nested in GET /v1alpha1/runs/{id}'s Run-view payload — newest-first by `updated_at`, using `node_runs_namespace_updated_at_idx` (migrations/0010) for the namespace scope, the `updated_since`/`updated_until` range, and the sort in one index walk.

Pagination is a keyset cursor (`cursor`/`next_cursor`), not OFFSET: `updated_at` changes on every node run's state transition — including rows outside the caller's current page — so an OFFSET-based page would silently skip or repeat rows as items elsewhere in the namespace move past the offset boundary between two requests. A cursor anchored to `(updated_at, id)` of the last row already served has no such failure mode and reuses the same index walk a first page already does. Pass `next_cursor` from a response back as `cursor` to fetch the next page; its absence means there is no further page.

post.description: Consumes every active token, marks every non-terminal node run and ready work item cancelled, and moves the run to `cancelled` — under the same per-run advisory lock the engine's own completion transaction takes (PRD §12.5), so a cancel cannot interleave with a concurrent attempt completion. A node run a worker already holds a lease on finishes that lease's fenced completion path (it will find the node run terminal and no-op); cancellation does not reach into an in-flight attempt.

409.description: The run has already reached a terminal state.

get.description:
Streams only committed events (PRD §15.1 CloudEvents-compatible envelopes), polling the events table every 500ms for rows newer than the resume point. Resume by per-run sequence: send `Last-Event-ID` (a previously received `id:` field) to resume after a disconnect, or the `from` query parameter for a client that cannot set headers before its first connection. Each frame is `id: <sequence>
event: <type>
data: <envelope JSON>

`. The stream ends (the connection closes normally) once a terminal run event (`run.completed`, `run.failed`, `run.cancelled`, or `run.bounded`) has been sent, since no further event will ever be appended for this run.

post.description: Compiles the submitted source and, if it compiles cleanly, stores it as an immutable workflow version addressed by its content digest (PRD §11.3). Publishing the same content twice is idempotent: the existing version is returned with `200 OK` rather than a conflict, because a digest is a statement about content, not about who asked first.

post.description: Runs the PRD §11.4 validation levels over the submitted source and returns every diagnostic. This never persists anything — a document with error diagnostics is a documented domain outcome (`valid: false` with an empty digest), not an HTTP error, matching the `nodes validate` CLI verb (PRD §3.4: a domain outcome is not a technical failure).

200.description: The document was compiled. `valid` reports whether it has any error diagnostic.

400.description: The request itself is malformed (missing source, unknown format).
